gap: No result ChatGPT got states which silent switch set fits which low-profile board: that Lofree sells its Void silent linear switches as a separate $59 set, and that (per Greenkeys' Ryosuke Kawamura) they fit Lofree's earlier Flow / Flow Lite hot-swap boards and Choc V2-standard sockets but not NuPhy's Air series (Gateron LP 3.0/2.0).
standout_why: Compared against mkbguide.com and keyboardranker.com (both cited), plus theofficejournal.com and keyboardverdict.com. The two cited rtings.com best-of pages returned only navigation to my fetches, so I could not compare against them. mkbguide already says the NuPhy Air75 V3's 'low-profile sockets limit later switch choices to the low-profile ecosystem' and lists the Flow 2 84 (Void) as hot-swap with VIA. keyboardranker already maps one silent switch to one board family (Keychron Silent K Pro for the V Max series). None names the Void set as a separate purchase or says Lofree's Kailh-pattern and NuPhy's Gateron-pattern low-profile switches do not interchange. The score stays at 1 because the cross-fit statement comes from a named third party, not Lofree: every maker product page (lofree.co, nuphy.com, gamakay.com, keychron.com) returned HTTP 429 on each attempt today.
decides: It confirms rather than changes the pick. A shopper who wants a silent low-profile board from our links should buy the Flow 2 84 in the Void variant; no rival says a cheaper Lofree board can be converted with the $59 Void set, and I could not confirm that from Lofree either. It also means a NuPhy Air75 V3 (ChatGPT's 'best overall') and a Lofree board cannot share silent switches, per Greenkeys, so the switch choice is locked to the brand's socket pattern at purchase. Treat the Flow Lite 2 84 conversion as unproven until Lofree's Void page is read.
